Feature demo · v0.5.0

External link icons

This page uses the theme's real module, component CSS and SVG partials. It marks links that leave the publication, leaves internal and non-web links alone, and checks its own result against the rules.

Both panels show the same markup with a forced colour scheme, so you can compare light and dark side by side. Hover or tab to a link to see the icon reach full ink. The panel content is not a Ghost install — the theme is the same one the demo publications run.

Light scheme

Forced light

The theme classifies every link inside .gh-content after Ghost renders it. A relative internal link stays in this tab. A GitHub link gets the GitHub mark and opens in a new tab. A host the theme does not recognize gets the generic external mark.

Existing rel tokens survive: this link keeps nofollow sponsored and gains noopener noreferrer. Subdomains resolve too: it.wikipedia.org uses the Wikipedia icon, and open.spotify.com uses Spotify. An absolute URL to this same page is internal.

Unknown hosts get the generic mark. Mastodon is federated and deliberately generic: it has no single domain.

Result on this page

Running…

The page checks every example after the module runs.

What the module does

It runs on a post or page only. It reads every a[href] inside .gh-content, resolves the URL against the page, accepts only http: and https:, normalizes www. on both sides, and compares the hosts. Same host: no change. Different host: one icon, target="_blank", noopener noreferrer merged with the existing rel, and a visually hidden “Opens in a new tab” label.

The icon is decorative (aria-hidden), inherits currentColor, sits at 55% opacity at rest, reaches full opacity on hover and keyboard focus, and is hidden in print. There is never more than one icon.

Recognized services

A service matches its exact domain or a subdomain. The most specific domain wins, so open.spotify.com uses Spotify and aws.amazon.com uses Amazon. Everything else gets the generic Feather external-link mark.
